claim: The executor builds each handler's bundle exactly as it builds every other bundle
why: src/executor.jl:237-242: make_handler_bundle expands the same _bundle_expr(BN, XT, ...) that every entry uses (executor.jl:128-143), at dispatch, from the live store. The one difference is the gather_input_barrier function barrier (store.jl:100), which the update entry also uses (executor.jl:160-164). It is a compile-cost device with the same values, so the bundle's content and source are the same as every other bundle's.

claim: The two arms are `y_state(c::AbstractLinearSystem{false}, (; x)) = C x` and `y_direct(c::AbstractLinearSystem{true}, (; x, u)) = C x + D u`
why: src/library.jl:1054-1058 y_state(c::AbstractLinearSystem{false}, (; x)) and y_direct(c::AbstractLinearSystem{true}, (; x, u)) on the supertype. | Section 3 writes the bodies in math notation (C x, C x + D u). The code wraps them in as_port/as_vector, which section 4 describes. As a schematic the arms match. Section 6's Julia block is judged separately under K6c-045.

claim: A declared period would need a hook that `sample_times` deliberately denies instances (D-042)
why: src/declare.jl:492-493 sample_times returns the assembly's map of immediate child name to Relative/Absolute, and 504 'The rates belong to the assembly type'; spec §8.7 (design/spec.md:4428-4432) rules that the declaration belongs to the assembly type, not the child instance, and rejects instance wrappers (D-042). | No hook lets a leaf instance declare its own period. One reading needs care: the sample_times docstring (src/declare.jl:505-506) lets an assembly read a deployment-preference rate off its own instance. That is the parent's instance, not the child's, so the claim stands.

claim: A static `exp` takes about 41 ns at 4x4 and 125 ns at 5x5 on Julia 1.13.1
why: probe.jl:114 and probe.jl:127, on Julia 1.13.3: a static exp allocates 0 B at every size probed. Augmented hold matrices at Δt = 0.01 take about 80 ns at 4x4 and 145 ns at 5x5; random 4x4/5x5 matrices take about 100 and 257-377 ns. | The measurement is tied to the machine and to Julia 1.13.1, and W runs 1.13.3. The zero allocation and the order of magnitude reproduce. The exact 41 ns and 125 ns do not: my 4x4 figure is about twice the doc's. Other sessions may have been loading the CPU during the probe.

claim: A tick's publication already allocates hundreds of bytes
why: probe.jl:106 gives boundary! of a discrete hold 0 B; probe.jl:108 gives one frame of step! 1,024 B; probe.jl:101 gives about 880 B per frame over 0.1 s; test/test_localization.jl:392-405 pins that the frame loop allocates its publications and nothing else. | Publications are per frame, not per discrete tick. In this deployment tick and frame coincide. 'Hundreds of bytes' holds.

claim: that companion's cascade table ranks tracking alone as the weakest variant and hold with tracking as the best
why: Probe out.txt:50-55 reproduces pid_anti_windup.md's cascade table at W: none 8.33/38.5, hold 6.10/32.5, tracking Tt=2 6.13/25.8, tracking Tt=0.5 7.27/55.2, both Tt=2 5.20/26.9, both Tt=0.5 5.09/22.0. That companion ranks them in the prose under its table at lines 310-314 ('The hold alone beats ungated tracking at its better Tt, and the two together beat both'), and D-383's Rejected list says the same. | The ranking is by peak. On settling time alone, tracking at Tt = 2 (25.8 s) beats the hold (32.5 s).

claim: switchover bump 1.92 with tracking always, Tt = 1
why: Probe out.txt:6: siblings with DiscretePID tracking = true, Tt = 1 (both siblings tracking always) give a bump of 1.9191, which rounds to 1.92.

claim: u_raw = v + Tt Ki e in standby is most of the 1.92 bump
why: Probe out.txt:13: after 2 s in standby with tracking always and Tt = 1, a's u_raw - v = 1.923, which is the 1.92 bump, and Tt Ki e = 1.438. The bias accounts for about three quarters of the bump, and the rest is lag behind the moving target. The discrete fixed point dt Ki e / beta gives about 1.445.

Probe out.txt:33 computes it from the inverse and K alone. src/library.jl:2905 takes K_fwd as a designed keyword, consistent with keeping it outside. | Read as 'needs no Riccati solve beyond K, which the tracker already has', the claim holds, and D-383's Rejected list uses the same wording ('the feedforward needs only an inverse').
